desc: Acceptance tests that only type-check money fields leave the ticket amount matrix unenforced so wrong prices still pass.
Fixture tests that ignore category fields allow staple and fresh labels to invert without failing the gate.
Basket membership checks that use sku id sets alone do not enforce required quantities.
Offer fixture tests that lock only minima leave day lists categories bank product and provenance fields free to drift.
Image fixture tests that check only PNG magic bytes and size do not enforce required visible text in the sample receipt.
Server-rendered form state round-tripped through the browser is parsed without shape validation, so a tampered or malformed hidden field turns into a server error instead of being dropped.

Fallback and threshold behaviors named in the ticket, such as a failed live call keeping the sample data and low-confidence rows starting unchecked, ship without any test that would fail if they regressed.
Tests that fall back to an environment-selected model client will call a paid live API on any developer machine that exports credentials, so the suite must isolate itself from those variables.
Upstream model answers and unsupported uploads are trusted to have the expected shape, so a malformed answer or wrong file type surfaces as a server error instead of a typed client or gateway error.
An ignore rule that names one personal file by exact name leaves the next personal photo saved beside it unprotected, so ignore patterns should cover the class of file.
A live explanation call that fails upstream propagates as a server error even though a fully grounded fallback sentence can be built from the deterministic engine output without the model.
Judge-facing documentation describes interactions and runtime paths the shipped interface does not have, which overstates the product to the reader it is meant to convince.

A container check that only greps for required strings still passes when the image omits the data files the app loads at runtime, so it must also assert the copy and install steps that make those files reachable.
A graceful fallback that swallows an upstream failure without logging it leaves operators unable to tell a bad credential from a timeout in production.
A leak guard that compares identifying values case-sensitively misses the same value printed in a different case, so personal data can pass the guard it was meant to stop.
An optimizer that accepts non-positive quantities or negative costs from model-chosen tool arguments produces impossible plans, so engine inputs must be validated at the engine boundary.

SC-018 Why step: the explanation number filter allows numbers from every tool result, including explain_plan_numbers, which echoes numbers from a model-supplied plan, and plan_day error messages. Repro: a runner calling explain_plan_numbers({plan:{saving:98765}}) got 'Glomark saves you 98765 LKR' shown to the shopper. Only engine-computed tool outputs may widen the filter.

SC-018 POST /ui returns 500 on untrusted form state: trip_cost or budget 'inf' raises OverflowError in bounded_int, and a receipt_json row dated 9999-12-31 overflows the pantry due-date arithmetic. Repro via TestClient with those fields. The page must fall back to defaults instead.
SC-018 POST /ui decodes the body strictly as UTF-8, so a body with invalid bytes (action=plan&today=0xFF 0xFE) returns 500 instead of the page with defaults.

SC-018 Why step cuts each tool call's arguments at 300 characters with no marker, so a real plan_day call over the default 11-line basket is shown incomplete, against the ticket's 'every tool call with its arguments'.

SC-018 makes Explain this plan run a re-planning ADK agent (several Gemini calls per click) on a public no-login URL, with no rate limit on that path or on /v1/explain; only receipt extraction is limited. A script could run up model cost on the billed project. Fix: one process-wide cap on model explanation runs, falling back to the engine explanation.

SC-018 (cross-model review, Gemini): successful plan_day and get_pantry results echo model-chosen inputs (unknown sku ids in unpriced, unknown usual_store in baseline store_id, fractional qty digits, trip_cost_lkr, and days_left steered by the today argument), and every number in them widened the explanation filter. Repro: runner with plan_day(lines=[{sku_id:'unknown_98765', qty:1.77777}], usual_store='store_54321') showed 'You save 98765 LKR and 54321 LKR'.

SC-018 (cross-model review, Gemini): _replan_differences assumes well-typed plan_day call args; a model call with qty 'bad' or banks [null] raises ValueError/TypeError outside the agent try block, so POST /ui returns 500.

SC-021 (cross-model review, Gemini): offer-minimum suggestions checked the gap with shelf prices instead of the promoted prices the planner uses, and never checked that the card offer fires in the re-plan. Repro: Commercial Bank at Keells, flora x3 and bread x4 on Saturday: page claimed carrot plus red dhal reach the LKR 4,000 minimum while the re-planned bill was LKR 3,992 with no card.

SC-024 (cross-model, Gemini): validate_rule treats an out-of-range minimum (over LKR 1,000,000 or negative) as not stated and checks with none, accepts percent_off True as 1%, and slices a non-list excluded_items character by character ('g' excluded six gram items) or crashes POST /ui on a dict.

SC-024 (cross-model, Gemini): drop_swapped_roles looks only at the six words before a number, so '4609 LKR is your saving' is kept and correct sentences such as 'After the card discount, 4609 LKR is the total bill.' are dropped.
SC-024 (cross-model, Gemini): _held_plan adds the checked offer's bank to the wallet, unlocking that bank's other fixture offers, so a check paying LKR 0 claims 'LKR 578 less' when holding the card.
SC-024 (cross-model, Gemini): normalize_lines_v2 passes qty inf through, accepts booleans for qty and confidence, and inflates sub-gram quantities to 1.0.

SC-024 (cross-model, Gemini round 2): CLAUSE_BREAK split on ':' separated labels such as 'Plan total: 1331 LKR' from their numbers, missing that swap and dropping 'Total: 4609 LKR (saving: 1331 LKR).'

SC-026 (cross-model, Gemini): after_model_guard does not normalize thousands separators, so 'You save 4,609 LKR' escapes the swap guard, invented '2,609' passes when its digit groups are allowed, and grounded '1,331' is mangled.

SC-026 (cross-model, Gemini): check_card_offer and plan_day accept model-chosen lines (and plan_day a model-chosen trip cost), so quantities such as cheese x50 + milk powder x22.127 make eligible_lkr exactly 98765 and 'saves you 98765 LKR' reached the page; negative and NaN quantities are not refused.

SC-026 (cross-model, Gemini): after_model_guard filters each response part separately and ask_agent joins parts without spaces, so 'You save ' + '4609 LKR' fuses into 'save4609' past the swap guard, cross-part digits fuse into ungrounded numbers, and thought parts leak into the answer.
SC-026 (cross-model, Gemini): tidy_orphan_units removes a legitimate 'LKR' that had no number, e.g. 'Prices are in LKR.'

An older and more specific style rule silently cancelled a new minimum touch-target size, and the test only compared literal selector text instead of the effective cascade on the element users actually tap.
Collapsing a disclosure removed the only visible statement that some recommended offers are fictional, while a new prominent recommendation presented those offers as advice.
Moving solver details into a collapsed block removed the only visible signal that a plan was not proven optimal.
A demo page priced with fixed inputs showed a new household summary and an imperative recommendation built from different inputs, so the page contradicted itself.
The implementation invented an extra label variant for one item state instead of using the labels the spec enumerated, and the new test encoded the deviation instead of the spec.
Renaming a navigation control broke wording that a frozen walkthrough document tells reviewers to press, and left two identical primary controls on one page.
Repeated disclosure toggles shared identical accessible names with no reference to the row they belong to.
New interactive disclosure summaries were introduced below the minimum touch-target size in a change whose purpose was raising touch targets.
A new element reused a class name already styled as a grid for an unrelated component, coupling their styles.
Boundary labels, the zero-count summary, warning-state style rules, and scroll wrappers were never exercised by the tests, so mutants of each survived.
The build was verified against spec text edited after the human approval gate without a fresh approval.
An uncertainty qualifier was added to one surface that names an invented offer, but other surfaces naming the same offer were left unqualified after the explaining disclosure was collapsed.
A control label assumed one entry path into an optional side trip, so it read wrongly when the side trip was opened from an earlier step.
An uncertainty qualifier keyed on which options a result used missed other visible lines that name the same invented option, so its terms still read as fact.
A placement and absence test checked a generic closing tag and skipped one page, so a misplaced or false notice still passed.
A disclosure keyed on what the computed result used missed free-form model text that can describe any held option, so invented terms could still appear as fact.
Tests asserted a qualifier appears on invented items but never that it stays off genuine items, so over-labelling passed.
A disclosure was scoped to the options the user holds, but the model's tools can reach every option, so invented terms for unheld options still appeared unqualified.
Two conditions coincided in every test case, so a mutant keyed on the wrong condition survived.
A touch-target pass covered the main controls but missed a secondary form whose many inline checkboxes stayed small, and the browser measurement did not include checkboxes.
Prosecution convergence did not complete: the fifth and final allowed round still surfaced confirmed findings, so two consecutive dry rounds were never observed.
A disclosure about model actions counted refused or failed tool calls as completed actions, so the page claimed something happened that did not.
A fixed table layout with non-wrapping headers let header text overflow into neighbouring columns on narrow screens, which a page-width check could not detect.
Per-row assertions sat inside a loop over regex matches with no check that any row matched, so markup drift silently skipped them.
A re-baseline changed the figure a negative assertion searched for, leaving the assertion unable to fail.
Rounding tests used no tie values that distinguish half-up from half-to-even, and typed pack amounts were not exercised.
An input step shared by two item kinds invited amounts one kind silently rounds away without telling the user.
Order-based pairing of tool calls with their responses was only tested with a single call, so mispairing mutants survived.
A notice that echoes rejected model input had no test proving the input is escaped.
Retried identical refused calls each produced a duplicate disclosure notice.
A verification step quoted a changed-line count that a later spec revision made stale.
Separate disclosure lists for failed and completed attempts produced contradictory notices when a failed call was retried successfully.
A pairing test placed its decoy where mispairing changed nothing observable, so the mutant it targeted still survived.
Deduplication keyed on rendered text and applied to both outcome kinds merged distinct attempts beyond what the spec allowed.
Two requests were judged the same or different by comparing lossy display text instead of normalised arguments, so retries and distinct attempts were confused.
New tests ran many requests against a process-wide per-minute cap and silently exhausted it for later tests, making failures depend on test order.
Two comparisons of the same inputs used different equality rules (numeric versus textual), so one judged a retry identical and the other did not.
A request identity kept duplicates the downstream tool merges, so equivalent requests looked different.
A new helper assumed untrusted arguments were an object and crashed the page on other shapes, regressing earlier tolerance.
Tests checked only the kind of each notice, never its text or the normalisation rules, so several normalisation mutants survived.
Merged quantities were rounded per row before summing, unlike the downstream planner, so equal baskets could differ and different ones match.
A number check compared a formatted value with its repr, so some genuine numbers were classified as malformed.
A rewritten branch for malformed rows had no test, so a mutant that silently dropped them survived.
Prosecution convergence did not complete: the fifth and final allowed round still surfaced confirmed findings, so two consecutive dry rounds were never observed.
A confirm form could not express a restriction the reader had found, so resubmitting it silently widened an offer to the whole bill.
An unvalidated client field was used to extend an engine input, so a tampered value crashed the page.
A response cache key left out part of the model's tool context, so different sessions could share an answer.
Two totals on one page used different formulas and disagreed.
A notice stated a reason the engine never computed when an option was not used.
Lenient date parsing dropped printed years and accepted unrelated words, reviving expired terms.
A substring heuristic classified issuers as card networks and implied wider eligibility.
A hidden field length cap below the escaped size of valid input silently dropped the carried state.
Results of time-limited solves were cached forever, freezing an unproven answer.
New tests passed against several mutants of the claimed behaviour, including a tamper rejected for the wrong reason.
